[standards/technology/ai/STD-TEC-AI-006-ai-agent-telemetry.md#purpose-statement]

### Purpose Statement

This standard ensures that every enterprise AI agent in Pilot or Production state is observable, supportable, and measurable. It defines mandatory operational metadata, required metrics, alerting and escalation requirements, and support model requirements that agents must meet to maintain their Production lifecycle state.
page_texts.5:
[standards/technology/ai/STD-TEC-AI-006-ai-agent-telemetry.md#scope]

### Scope

This standard applies to all AI Agents (Configured) and Custom AI Agents in Pilot and Production lifecycle states. Proposed and Retired capabilities are excluded, though documentation of historical operational metadata for Retired capabilities is required per STD-GOV-AI-005.
page_texts.6:
[standards/technology/ai/STD-TEC-AI-006-ai-agent-telemetry.md#compliance-level]

### Compliance Level

Mandatory. All Pilot and Production agents must publish the required operational metadata and metrics before or at Pilot promotion.
page_texts.7:
[standards/technology/ai/STD-TEC-AI-006-ai-agent-telemetry.md#business-rationale]

### Business Rationale

Federated AI agent portfolios become opaque without standard telemetry conventions. When an agent produces a compliance incident, a support request, or a quality regression, the organization must be able to identify the agent version, owner, last validation state, and usage patterns. Without mandatory telemetry, operational and compliance issues cannot be investigated, and governance decisions cannot be made with evidence.

page_texts.9:
[standards/technology/ai/STD-TEC-AI-006-ai-agent-telemetry.md#mandatory-requirements]

### Mandatory Requirements

**Mandatory Operational Metadata:**

Every Pilot and Production capability must maintain and publish the following:

1. Owner and backup owner — named individuals with confirmed availability
2. Support contact path — the channel or process through which users can report issues or request help
3. Lifecycle state — current state from the lifecycle state model defined in STD-TEC-AI-001
4. Version — current version per the naming convention in STD-TEC-AI-007
5. Last change date — the date the most recent change was made to the agent's prompts, configuration, or evidence connections
6. Last validation date — the date the agent's quality rubric was most recently evaluated

**Mandatory Metrics:**

At minimum, the following metrics must be collected and made available for monthly domain scorecard reporting:

1. Usage volume — total interaction count over the reporting period
2. Unique user adoption — count of distinct users who interacted with the agent over the reporting period
3. Output acceptance rate — proportion of outputs that users accepted without modification or rejection
4. Manual rework rate — proportion of outputs that required user modification before use
5. Defect rate by severity — count of defects reported, categorized by severity per the defect taxonomy in STD-TEC-AI-005
6. Policy compliance incident count — count of incidents in which the agent produced an output that violated a policy requirement
7. Time-to-resolution for incidents — elapsed time from incident report to confirmed resolution

**Alerting and Escalation Requirements:**

- Define thresholds for defect spikes and policy compliance incidents that trigger an alert
- Define an escalation path by incident severity tier — who is notified, in what sequence, and with what response time expectation
- Define containment criteria — the threshold conditions that trigger automatic or manual containment of the capability

**Support Model Requirements:**

- Defined triage workflow: the steps followed when a user reports an issue with the agent
- Defined ownership by defect class: which team or role is responsible for each defect class in the defect taxonomy
- Defined service targets: expected response time and resolution time by incident severity
- Defined user communication process: how users are notified of known issues and expected resolution timelines

**Reporting Requirements:**

- Monthly domain scorecard: all mandatory metrics reported at the domain level
- Quarterly enterprise portfolio scorecard: aggregate mandatory metrics across all Production capabilities
- Event-driven incident report: for any incident involving a high-severity policy compliance failure or extended service degradation
page_texts.10:
[standards/technology/ai/STD-TEC-AI-006-ai-agent-telemetry.md#recommended-practices]

### Recommended Practices

- Establish baseline metric values at Pilot so that Production deviations are detectable from day one
- Align metric collection with the platform's native analytics where available; supplement with manual reporting processes where platform observability is limited
- Communicate known issues to affected users proactively rather than waiting for reports
page_texts.11:
[standards/technology/ai/STD-TEC-AI-006-ai-agent-telemetry.md#prohibited-practices]

### Prohibited Practices

- Agents must not enter Production state without the mandatory operational metadata published in the capability registry
- Agents with no defined support contact path must not be in Production or Pilot state
page_texts.12:
[standards/technology/ai/STD-TEC-AI-006-ai-agent-telemetry.md#exceptions-process]

### Exceptions Process

1. Requests to defer mandatory metric collection at Pilot promotion require architecture board approval with a defined remediation date
2. Metric thresholds for alerting and escalation must be defined before Production promotion; they may not be deferred

---
page_texts.15:
[standards/technology/ai/STD-TEC-AI-006-ai-agent-telemetry.md#metric-collection-implementation]

#### Metric Collection Implementation

- For configured agents on M365 Copilot and Copilot Studio: collect available platform analytics (usage volume, adoption) and supplement with manual process tracking for metrics not available natively (rework rate, policy compliance incidents)
- For custom AI agents: implement metric collection in the agent application layer; all seven mandatory metrics must be collectable from the application instrumentation
page_texts.16:
[standards/technology/ai/STD-TEC-AI-006-ai-agent-telemetry.md#operational-metadata-publication]

#### Operational Metadata Publication

- Operational metadata must be published in the capability registry and kept current; stale metadata (older than one review cycle without update) constitutes non-compliance
- Changes to owner or backup owner must be reflected in the registry within five business days of the change taking effect
page_texts.17:
[standards/technology/ai/STD-TEC-AI-006-ai-agent-telemetry.md#alerting-threshold-configuration]

#### Alerting Threshold Configuration

- Alert thresholds must be specific numeric or rate values; thresholds expressed as "high" or "unusual" without quantification do not satisfy the requirement
- Escalation paths must name specific roles, not generic functions; "the team" does not satisfy the requirement

---
page_texts.20:
[standards/technology/ai/STD-TEC-AI-006-ai-agent-telemetry.md#phase-1-telemetry-setup-at-pilot-promotion]

#### Phase 1: Telemetry Setup (At Pilot Promotion)

1. Publish all mandatory operational metadata in the capability registry
2. Establish metric collection for all seven mandatory metrics using available platform analytics and supplemental process tracking
3. Define alert thresholds, escalation paths, and containment criteria
4. Define the support model (triage workflow, ownership by defect class, service targets, user communication process)
page_texts.21:
[standards/technology/ai/STD-TEC-AI-006-ai-agent-telemetry.md#phase-2-baseline-establishment-during-pilot]

#### Phase 2: Baseline Establishment (During Pilot)

1. Collect all seven mandatory metrics throughout the Pilot period
2. Record baseline metric values at the end of the Pilot period
3. Confirm that alert thresholds and containment criteria are correctly calibrated against the Pilot baseline before Production promotion
page_texts.22:
[standards/technology/ai/STD-TEC-AI-006-ai-agent-telemetry.md#phase-3-production-operations]

#### Phase 3: Production Operations

1. Produce monthly domain scorecard including all mandatory metrics
2. Conduct weekly operational review for any active incidents
3. Recalibrate metric thresholds and support service targets quarterly
page_texts.23:
[standards/technology/ai/STD-TEC-AI-006-ai-agent-telemetry.md#validation-criteria]

### Validation Criteria

| Validation Area | Criteria | Verification Method | Evidence Required |
| --------------- | --------- | ------------------- | -------------------- |
| Operational metadata completeness | All 6 mandatory metadata fields present and current in registry | Registry audit | Capability registry record |
| Metric collection | All 7 mandatory metrics are being collected and are available for reporting | Metric source review | Metric collection documentation |
| Alert thresholds defined | Numeric thresholds defined for defect spikes and compliance incidents | Threshold review | Alert threshold configuration |
| Support model defined | Triage workflow, ownership, service targets, and communication process documented | Support model review | Support model document |

---
page_texts.25:
[standards/technology/ai/STD-TEC-AI-006-ai-agent-telemetry.md#non-compliance-handling]

### Non-Compliance Handling

- Missing mandatory metrics at Production promotion: block promotion until metrics are collectable
- No owner or support path: move to Contained state
- Persistent threshold breaches without remediation plan: mandatory architecture board review
page_texts.26:
[standards/technology/ai/STD-TEC-AI-006-ai-agent-telemetry.md#governance-oversight]

### Governance Oversight

- **Standards Owner**: Enterprise Copilot Architecture Board
- **Compliance Manager**: Platform Governance Team (monthly operational metadata currency check)
- **Governance Body**: Enterprise Copilot Architecture Board (metric deferral exceptions; persistent breach escalation)
